newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Ex-Khmer Rouge general criticises Cambodia coup.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Khmer Rouge general criticises Cambodia coup.

text.p: A former Khmer Rouge general on Friday opposed the nomination of Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot as a replacement of ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

General Ei Chian, commander of the Democratic National United Movement (DNUM) of more than 3,000 armed Khmer Rouge dissidents in this western town, said the move to replace Ranariddh was inappropriate.
"For me and our movement, I oppose the appointment of Ung Huot," Ei Chian told Reuters in this gem-mining town near the border with Thailand.

He called on the international community and the United Nations to step in to help restore peace in Cambodia, which has been rocked by violence and political turmoil since Second Prime Minister Hun Sen deposed Ranariddh early this month.
"The U.N. should help us cope with the chaos and organise the next general election. Without the U.N., the election will be meaningless," he said.

The United Nations sponsored Cambodia's last general election in 1993 which led to the establishment of a shaky ruling coalition between Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party and Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party.

The DNUM was formed in August last year when former Khmer Rouge foreign minister Ieng Sary broke from the hardline, Maoist guerrilla group blamed for the deaths of more than one million Cambodians during their 1975-1979 "killing fields" rule.
"We oppose Ung Huot's nomination as it is not right. The political situation will return to normal only if the United Nations steps in," Ei Chian said at this former Khmer Rouge stronghold.
Ung Huot was nominated by remnants of Ranariddh's party for the first prime minister's post in a decision supported by Hun Sen.
Ei Chian condemned Hun Sen's removal of Ranariddh, saying it had harmed an already suffering country further.

"I am very disappointed and upset by developments in Phnom Penh. There should not be bloodshed like this. What happened in Cambodia in the past two weeks has driven away foreign investors and friends coming to help develop the economy," Ei Chian said.
Before the July 5-6 coup, the Cambodian government scheduled a general election for next May. Hun Sen has pledged to hold the election.

Ei Chian said Ranariddh could use Pailin as a springboard for advancing on the important town of Battambang, in northwest Cambodia, if the prince won support of the United Nations and the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
"He can use Pailin as an entry point if the U.N. and ASEAN backed him," Ei Chian said.
Pailin's population surged to 50,000 from 15,000 after DUNM took control of the town.
